Yeah, I guess we're going to have to agree to disagree about that.

The thing is, I don't see the mail as the SCP, but the site. The mail, really, is incidental and containable, and I don't think it's the purpose of the article to go into depths with the mail. Now, perhaps a supplemental log of interesting tidbits, I could see that, although that veers more toward Foundation Tales to my way of thinking.

The mail, really, should get you to wonder what could have been sent through the system. Think of the warehouse at the end of Raiders of the Lost Ark. I personally think that specific examples would weaken it. But that's just me.

Thanks for the feedback, though, it is appreciated.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay, that big question? That's beyond the purview of the article to answer, since this is an article about the containment procedures. But let's use a hypothetical situation.

Let's say that in 1999, a letter was received with the appropriate code-phrase and markings from 14 September, 2001. In it, there is information about 9/11, with the edict that all information the Foundation has stored in the World Trade Center is to be backed up and taken to Site 17 at the end of business, 10 September, 2001. Nothing about saving personnel, mind you, just the information.

Imagine the havoc that could be caused by the Foundation knowing about the events two years beforehand. That's why it's Overseers only, to minimize temporal disruption.

Occasionally, orders like that will be given and directed as stated. However, the Foundation is a profoundly paranoid organization, and as such has a variety of safeguards in place to minimize such shenanigans. Again, that's beyond the article's purview, but I should at least be hinting at that sort of thinking and double-thinking here, no?

item.title: The post office.
item.content:encoded:
This one I got the idea from when finishing up Ear Candles. The notion of an "Undead Letter Office" just seemed so fitting, but I wanted this to be different than other things out there. I was concerned about the similarities to the "New Pie" from Pratchett's Going Postal, but this place is significantly different from that. Photo started really liking the outline when we were chatting about it, and so here it is.

I hope you enjoy it.
